These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be in you, and your joy may be filled.

The Lord is gracious and merciful: patient and plenteous in mercy.

Come to me all you that labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you.

Judge not: and you shall not be judged. Condemn not: and you shall not be condemned. Forgive: and you shall be forgiven.

Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom.

Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the land.

Because the Lord giveth wisdom: and out of his mouth cometh prudence and knowledge.

And Jesus saith to them: Why are you fearful, O ye of little faith? Then rising up, he commanded the winds, and the sea, and there came a great calm.

Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.

Thus saith the Lord of hosts, saying: Judge ye true judgment, and shew ye mercy and compassion every man to his brother.

Better is the end of a speech than the beginning. Better is the patient man than the presumptuous.

Death and life are in the power of the tongue: they that love it, shall eat the fruits thereof.

Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering (for he is faithful that hath promised).

For in thee, O Lord, have I hoped: thou wilt hear me, O Lord my God.

Jesus saith to him: Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen and have believed.

When the ways of man shall please the Lord, he will convert even his enemies to peace.

He that feareth man shall quickly fall: he that trusteth in the Lord, shall be set on high.

Be subject to the Lord and pray to him. Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.

Therefore, whilst we have time, let us work good to all men, but especially to those who are of the household of the faith.

But without faith it is impossible to please God. For he that cometh to God must believe that he is: and is a rewarder to them that seek him.

Take up my yoke upon you, and learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart: And you shall find rest to your souls.

Go then, and eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with gladness: because thy works please God.

Be instant in prayer: watching in it with thanksgiving.

Casting all your care upon him, for he hath care of you.

Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out devils: freely have you received, freely give.

Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

The just shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow up like the cedar of Libanus.

And the peace of God, which surpasseth all understanding, keep your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.

But having food and wherewith to be covered, with these we are content.

If then any be in Christ a new creature, the old things are passed away. Behold all things are made new.

From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord.

Rooted and built up in him and confirmed in the faith, as also you have learned: abounding in him in thanksgiving.

Watch ye: stand fast in the faith: do manfully and be strengthened.

Owe no man any thing, but to love one another. For he that loveth his neighbour hath fulfilled the law.

But thou when thou shalt pray, enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father in secret, and thy father who seeth in secret will repay thee.

When thou shalt pour out thy soul to the hungry, and shalt satisfy the afflicted soul, then shall thy light rise up in darkness, and thy darkness shall be as the noonday.

But Jesus having heard the word that was spoken, saith to the ruler of the synagogue: Fear not, only believe.
For everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted.
Because every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled: and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
The beginning of wisdom is to obtain wisdom, and, with all that you possess, to acquire prudence.
The beginning of wisdom, get wisdom, and with all thy possession purchase prudence.

All whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
Rejoice always.
Always rejoice.
But piety with sufficiency is great gain.
But godliness with contentment is great gain.
But I will always have hope. And I will add more to all your praise.
But I will always hope; and will add to all thy praise.
O Lord, station a guard over my mouth and a door enclosing my lips.
Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth: and a door round about my lips.

And for raiment why are you solicitous? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they labour not, neither do they spin. But I say to you, that not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed as one of these.
By wisdom shall a house be built, and by prudence shall it be strengthened.
By wisdom the house shall be built, and by prudence it shall be strengthened.
But, before all things, have a constant mutual charity among yourselves. For love covers a multitude of sins.
But before all things have a constant mutual charity among yourselves: for charity covereth a multitude of sins.
Whoever speaks a word at an opportune time is like apples of gold on beds of silver.
To speak a word in due time, is like apples of gold on beds of silver.
Our God is our refuge and strength, a helper in the tribulations that have greatly overwhelmed us.
Our God is our refuge and strength: a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

But Jesus turning and seeing her, said: Be of good heart, daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.

He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in that which is greater: and he that is unjust in that which is little is unjust also in that which is greater.
Our soul remains with the Lord. For he is our helper and protector.
Our soul waiteth for the Lord: for he is our helper and protector.
This has consoled me in my humiliation, for your word has revived me.
This hath comforted me in my humiliation: because thy word hath enlivened me.

The learning of a man is known by patience: and his glory is to pass over wrongs.
You have trusted in the Lord for all eternity, in the Lord God almighty forever.
You have hoped in the Lord for evermore, in the Lord God mighty for ever.
Many men are called merciful. But who will find a faithful man?
Many men are called merciful: but who shall find a faithful man?
Therefore, confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be saved. For the unremitting prayer of a just person prevails over many things.
Confess therefore your sins one to another: and pray one for another, that you may be saved. For the continual prayer of a just man availeth much.
Fear is not in love. Instead, perfect love casts out fear, for fear pertains to punishment. And whoever fears is not perfected in love.
Fear is not in charity: but perfect charity casteth out fear, because fear hath sin. And he that feareth is not perfected in charity.
If it is possible, in so far as you are able, be at peace with all men.
If it be possible, as much as is in you, have peace with all men.

For thou, O God, hast proved us: thou hast tried us by fire, as silver is tried.
This is the day that the Lord has made. Let us exult and rejoice in it.
This is the day which the Lord hath made: let us be glad and rejoice therein.

And one of them, when he saw that he was made clean, went back, with a loud voice glorifying God. And he fell on his face before his feet, giving thanks. And this was a Samaritan.

And now what is my hope? is it not the Lord? and my substance is with thee.

For also, when we were with you, this we declared to you: that, if any man will not work, neither let him eat.
Pray without ceasing.
Pray without ceasing.
Behold, I am accomplishing new things. And presently, they will spring forth. With certainty, you will know them. I will make a way in the desert, and rivers in an impassible place.
Behold I do new things, and now they shall spring forth, verily you shall know them: I will make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

Say to the fainthearted: Take courage, and fear not: behold your God will bring the revenge of recompense: God himself will come and will save you.

And rising very early, going out, he went into a desert place: and there he prayed.

I will give praise to thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: I will relate all thy wonders.
And you, brothers, do not grow weak in doing good.
But you, brethren, be not weary in well doing.

And he that sat on the throne, said: Behold, I make all things new. And he said to me: Write. For these words are most faithful and true.

And thy ears shall hear the word of one admonishing thee behind thy back: This is the way, walk ye in it: and go not aside neither to the right hand, nor to the left.
For the earth bears fruit readily: first the plant, then the ear, next the full grain in the ear.
For the earth of itself bringeth forth fruit, first the blade, then the ear, afterwards the full corn in the ear.

In all things we suffer tribulation: but are not distressed. We are straitened: but are not destitute. We suffer persecution: but are not forsaken. We are cast down: but we perish not.
Turn again, my soul, to your rest. For the Lord has done good to you.
Turn, O my soul, into thy rest: for the Lord hath been bountiful to thee.

He that walketh with the wise, shall be wise: a friend of fools shall become like to them.
Rejoice in the Lord always. Again, I say, rejoice.
Rejoice in the Lord always: again, I say, rejoice.

Let no temptation take hold on you, but such as is human. And God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that which you are able: but will make also with temptation issue, that you may be able to bear it.

I will be as the dew, Israel shall spring as the lily, and his root shall shoot forth as that of Libanus.

Let no evil speech proceed from your mouth: but that which is good, to the edification of faith: that it may administer grace to the hearers.

Finally, brethren, be strengthened in the Lord and in the might of his power.

Caph. For if he hath cast off, he will also have mercy, according to the multitude of his mercies.

And the fruit of justice is sown in peace, to them that make peace.

But above all these things have charity, which is the bond of perfection.

For to you, I will pray. In the morning, Lord, you will hear my voice.
For to thee will I pray: O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.

And which of you by taking thought can add to his stature one cubit?

Expect the Lord, do manfully, and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.
For you will have hope in the end, and your expectation will not be taken away.
Because thou shalt have hope in the latter end, and thy expectation shall not be taken away.

The Lord God is my strength: and he will make my feet like the feet of harts: and he the conqueror will lead me upon my high places singing psalms.

Again therefore, Jesus spoke to: them, saying: I am the light of the world. He that followeth me walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
The love of neighbor does no harm. Therefore, love is the plenitude of the law.
The love of our neighbour worketh no evil. Love therefore is the fulfilling of the law.

Therefore, neither he that planteth is any thing, nor he that watereth: but God that giveth the increase.

Even so the tongue is indeed a little member and boasteth great things. Behold how small a fire kindleth a great wood.

I know, O Lord, that the way of a man is not his: neither is it in a man to walk, and to direct his steps.

It is better to be humbled with the meek, than to divide spoils with the proud.
Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my paths.
Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths.
He satisfies your desire with good things. Your youth will be renewed like that of the eagle.
Who satisfieth thy desire with good things: thy youth shall be renewed like the eagle's.

Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me, and with thy glory thou hast received me.
Go to the ant, you lazy one, and consider her ways, and so learn wisdom.
Go to the ant, O sluggard, and consider her ways, and learn wisdom.
Yet, truly, my soul will be subject to God. For from him is my patience.
But be thou, O my soul, subject to God: for from him is my patience.

When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me. Have mercy on me: and hear my prayer.

Say not: What thinkest thou is the cause that former times were better than they are now? for this manner of question is foolish.
For with you is the fountain of life; and within your light, we will see the light.
For with thee is the fountain of life; and in thy light we shall see light.
And we have known and believed the love that God has for us. God is love. And he who abides in love, abides in God, and God in him.
And we have known and have believed the charity which God hath to us. God is charity: and he that abideth in charity abideth in God, and God in him.
Better is a little with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures and dissatisfaction.
Better is a little with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures without content.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of holiness is prudence.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is prudence.
You have turned my mourning into gladness for me. You have cut off my sackcloth, and you have surrounded me with joy.
Thou hast turned for me my mourning into joy: thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness.

And be ye kind one to another: merciful, forgiving one another, even as God hath forgiven you in Christ.

And the apostles said to the Lord: Increase our faith.

Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing: that you may abound in hope and in the power of the Holy Ghost.

The Lord is compassionate and merciful: longsuffering and plenteous in mercy.

Better is a dry morsel with joy, than a house full of victims with strife.

Peace I leave with you: my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, do I give unto you. Let not your heart be troubled: nor let it be afraid.

For God hath not given us the spirit of fear: but of power and of love and of sobriety.

For thou, O Lord, art sweet and mild: and plenteous in mercy to all that call upon thee.

And as you would that men should do to you, do you also to them in like manner.

And when you shall stand to pray, forgive, if you have aught against any man: that your Father also, who is in heaven, may forgive you your sins.

For I am the Lord thy God, who take thee by the hand, and say to thee: Fear not, I have helped thee.
Be humbled in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.
Be humbled in the sight of the Lord: and he will exalt you.
It is better to be called to vegetables with charity, than to a fatted calf with hatred.
It is better to be invited to herbs with love, than to a fatted calf with hatred.
And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.
And the light shineth in darkness: and the darkness did not comprehend it.
Bless the Lord, O my soul, and do not forget all his recompenses.
Bless the Lord, O my soul, and never forget all he hath done for thee.
For judgment is without mercy toward him who has not shown mercy. But mercy exalts itself above judgment.
For judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy. And mercy exalteth itself above judgment.

Likewise, the Spirit also helpeth our infirmity. For, we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit himself asketh for us with unspeakable groanings.
For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but rather justice and peace and joy, in the Holy Spirit.
For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink: but justice and peace and joy in the Holy Ghost.
The fear of the Lord is the discipline of wisdom. And humility precedes glory.
The fear of the Lord is the lesson of wisdom: and humility goeth before glory.

But if any man have not care of his own and especially of those of his house, he hath denied the faith and is worse than an infidel.
A joyful soul makes a lifetime flourish. A gloomy spirit dries out the bones.
A joyful mind maketh age flourishing: a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones.
For you were darkness, in times past, but now you are light, in the Lord. So then, walk as sons of the light.
For you were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord. Walk then as children of the light.

Yet still, God, who is rich in mercy, for the sake of his exceedingly great charity with which he loved us, even when we were dead in our sins, has enlivened us together in Christ, by whose grace you have been saved.
But God (who is rich in mercy) for his exceeding charity wherewith he loved us Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together in Christ (by whose grace you are saved)
Whoever heeds the wind will not sow. And whoever considers the clouds will never reap.
He that observeth the wind, shall not sow: and he that considereth the clouds, shall never reap.
But I will look towards the Lord. I will wait for God, my Savior. My God will hear me.
But I will look towards the Lord, I will wait for God, my saviour: my God will hear me.
For we walk by means of faith, and not by sight.
(For we walk by faith and not by sight.)
And immediately, Jesus spoke to them, saying: “Have faith. It is I. Do not be afraid.”
And immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying: Be of good heart: it is I, fear ye not.
I will not leave you orphans. I will return to you.
I will not leave you orphans: I will come to you.
I have fought the good fight. I have completed the course. I have preserved the faith.
I have fought a good fight: I have finished my course: I have kept the faith.
But the path of the just is like a shining light: it advances and increases, even to the day of completion.
But the path of the just, as a shining light, goeth forwards, and increaseth even to perfect day.

And the Lord will give you rest continually, and he will fill your soul with splendor, and he will free your bones, and you will be like a watered garden and like a fountain of water whose waters will not fail.

And the Lord will give thee rest continually, and will fill thy soul with brightness, and deliver thy bones, and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a fountain of water whose waters shall not fail.
The Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my liberator. My God is my helper, and I hope in him: my protector, and the horn of my salvation, and my support.
The Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer. My God is my helper, and in him will I put my trust. My protector, and the horn of my salvation, and my support.
All things have their time, and all things under heaven continue during their interval.
All things have their season, and in their times all things pass under heaven.

Give, and it will be given to you: a good measure, pressed down and shaken together and overflowing, they will place upon your lap. Certainly, the same measure that you use to measure out, will be used to measure back to you again.

Give: and it shall be given to you: good measure and pressed down and shaken together and running over shall they give into your bosom. For with the same measure that you shall mete withal, it shall be measured to you again.
Careful words are a honeycomb: sweet to the soul and healthful to the bones.
Well ordered words are as a honeycomb: sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
Therefore, let us love God, for God first loved us.
Let us therefore love God: because God first hath loved us.
A faithful man shall be greatly praised. But whoever rushes to become rich will not be innocent.
A faithful man shall be much praised: but he that maketh haste to be rich, shall not be innocent.
For, even if I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils. For you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they have given me consolation.
For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, for thou art with me. Thy rod and thy staff, they have comforted me.
Lord, your mercy is in heaven, and your truth is even to the clouds.
O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven, and thy truth reacheth even to the clouds.
Evening and morning and midday, I will discourse and announce, and he will heed my voice.
Evening and morning, and at noon I will speak and declare: and he shall hear my voice.
The Lord is good to those who hope in him, to the soul that seeks him.
Teth. The Lord is good to them that hope in him, to the soul that seeketh him.

For if you will forgive men their offences, your heavenly Father will forgive you also your offences.
From ages past, they have not heard it, and they have not perceived it with the ears. Apart from you, O God, the eye has not seen what you have prepared for those who await you.
From the beginning of the world they have not heard, nor perceived with the ears: the eye hath not seen, O God, besides thee, what things thou hast prepared for them that wait for thee.
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. A light has risen for the inhabitants of the region of the shadow of death.
The people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light: to them that dwelt in the region of the shadow of death, light is risen.
The steps of a man will be directed by the Lord, and he will choose his way.
With the Lord shall the steps of a man be directed, and he shall like well his way.
For wrath is in his indignation, and life is in his will. Toward evening, weeping will linger, and toward morning, gladness.
For wrath is in his indignation; and life in his good will. In the evening weeping shall have place, and in the morning gladness.
Son, support your father in his old age, and do not grieve him in his life.
Son, support the old age of thy father, and grieve him not in his life.
Consider the birds of the air, how they neither sow, nor reap, nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of much greater value than they are?
Behold the birds of the air, for they neither sow, nor do they reap, nor gather into barns: and your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are not you of much more value than they?
You need not call to mind the past, nor consider the things of antiquity.
Remember not former things, and look not on things of old.
For I consider that the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with that future glory which shall be revealed in us.
For I reckon that the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us.

But within the wisdom that is from above, certainly, chastity is first, and next peacefulness, meekness, openness, consenting to what is good, a plenitude of mercy and good fruits, not judging, without falseness.
But the wisdom that is from above, first indeed is chaste, then peaceable, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good, full of mercy and good fruits, without judging, without dissimulation.
A little is better to the just than the many riches of sinners.
Better is a little to the just, than the great riches of the wicked.

The just shall be in everlasting remembrance: he shall not fear the evil hearing. His heart is ready to hope in the Lord.
If he would remain silent, even the foolish would be considered wise, and if he closes his lips, intelligent.
Even a fool, if he will hold his peace, shall be counted wise: and if he close his lips, a man of understanding.
